decisions.executionNote: Begin a small elbow-continuous right-arm approach; orient the gripper downward toward the set square, keeping clear of the cubes.
Approach above the right section of the set square while increasing downward pitch; keep the stationary left arm clear.
Continue pitching down over the right end, with small forward increments and clearance above the tool.
Finish the downward orientation and start turning the open jaws across the narrow set-square edge.
Turn the jaws across the set square while hovering, using only gradual wrist rotation.
Lower slowly toward the set-square right end and match jaw direction to its narrow cross-section; height remains visually uncertain.
Seat the open jaws a few millimeters lower around the tool, then close without lifting; assess contact from the next RGB view.
Test planar retention by gently straightening the set square and sliding it forward, with no upward motion near the cubes.
Advance the retained set square along the tabletop toward the nearest cube, gently correcting the remaining visible edge skew.
Push forward at a low, constant height with the straight edge approximately horizontal; monitor whether the nearest cube slides rather than lifts.
Continue the slow tabletop push to bring the middle block level with the outer two; the tool is sliding with some angular compliance.
Continue a gentle planar sweep until the leftmost cube also contacts the straight edge, matching the wrist slightly to the tool's observed angle.
The blocks now follow the edge but it is angled. Hold the right end still and approach the tool's left end within the left workspace to level the row.
Replan the rejected left approach from the unchanged pose using smaller translation and pitch increments; keep the right endpoint stationary.
Bring the left gripper above the free left section, gradually pitching down while keeping both elbows in the continuous upper configuration.
Continue the left downward approach above the tool's left section, keeping the right end and cubes still.
Finish the left downward pitch while rotating the jaws across the tool in the opposite, symmetric wrist orientation.
Rotate and lower the left open gripper toward the tool while retaining tabletop clearance and keeping the right arm stationary.
Place the left jaws around the left section at the proven low tool-contact height, completing the cross-edge orientation.
Close the left jaws around the tool without lifting, while the right arm holds its endpoint steady.
Advance only the left end along the tabletop and gently turn both wrists with the edge to reduce its angle and straighten the cube row.
Finish leveling the straight edge by advancing the left endpoint, with small wrist turns and no lift of the cubes.
The three cubes appear in a straight parallel row. Draw the straight edge slightly back, release it on the table, and start lifting only the empty grippers for reset.
Retract both open grippers away from the row and upward, unwinding wrist yaw along continuous elbow-up paths toward the starting poses.
Continue retreating symmetrically in the separate workspaces while unwinding yaw; the blocks and set square remain resting on the table.
Complete most wrist-yaw unwinding while moving rearward toward the original arm positions, leaving the aligned cubes untouched.
Pitch both empty grippers back toward their original forward orientation while smoothly retracting to the origin poses.
Continue the smooth reset trajectory, keeping both grippers open and the aligned row undisturbed.
Approach the original open-gripper poses with the same small continuous increments; inspect the remaining reset error next.
